questions.prompt: What does a reversible Boolean oracle preserve?

options.text: The input x while XORing f(x) into a helper
Only the helper while deleting x
A measured classical answer on every branch
The probability of every amplitude sign

questions.explanation: The interface keeps x and maps y to y XOR f(x), so it can be reversed.

questions.prompt: Which helper state makes an X flip appear as a phase?
questions.explanation: X|-> = -|->, so a conditional X transfers a minus sign to the input branch.

questions.prompt: What is the phase sign when f(x)=0?

options.text: It is undefined

questions.explanation: The phase factor is (-1)^f(x), which equals +1 when f(x)=0.

questions.prompt: For XOR in input order 00,01,10,11, which phase pattern does |-> produce?
questions.explanation: XOR is one on 01 and 10, so those branches get minus signs while 00 and 11 stay positive.

questions.prompt: Why is a phase-kickback helper not measured as the function answer?

options.text: It stores the signs while remaining in the same |-> state
It is always destroyed by the oracle
It contains no qubit
Measurement is not allowed in quantum circuits

questions.explanation: The helper is an X eigenstate. The function value appears as a sign on the input amplitudes, which later interference can use.

questions.prompt: What does one oracle query count?

options.text: Every elementary gate in the complete application
One invocation of the abstract U_f interface
One measured output bit
One classical truth-table row

questions.explanation: Query complexity treats the oracle as a higher-level interface. Its implementation still has gate and depth costs.

questions.prompt: For f(00)=1, f(01)=0, f(10)=1, f(11)=0, what signs appear with |->?
questions.explanation: The sign is negative exactly when f(x)=1, giving -, +, -, + in the listed order.

questions.prompt: Why can an immediate Z measurement fail to reveal phase kickback?

options.text: Negative amplitudes are not valid
Z measurement squares magnitudes, so relative signs need later interference
The oracle changes no state at all
The helper must be measured first

questions.explanation: Signs do not change the current Z-basis probabilities. A later basis change can combine paths and make them observable.

questions.prompt: Which statement is the fairest description of an oracle-model speedup?

options.text: One query means the real circuit has one gate
Query complexity ignores implementation cost entirely in every comparison
It compares calls to a defined interface, while construction and depth remain relevant
It guarantees a faster device for every truth table

questions.explanation: The oracle model isolates information access. A practical comparison must still account for compilation, ancillas, connectivity and noise.
